R0193.title: Blockchain Supply Chain Attack
R0193.definition: Attackers compromise blockchain development tools, SDKs, wallet plugins and other supply chain components to inject malicious code, affecting numerous downstream projects and users.

references.title: 2025 Web3 Security Annual Report: Supply Chain Attacks Become the Largest Threat
Blockchain Security: Preventing Threats Before They Strike

R0193.description:
Blockchain supply chain attacks target development tools, wallet plugins, SDKs, node components, frontend dependencies, and release processes. Attackers tamper with dependencies, insert backdoors, or take over publisher accounts to deliver malicious logic to downstream Web3 projects.

Because Web3 applications directly handle keys, signatures, and on-chain assets, supply chain compromise can trigger asset theft, authorization tampering, or sensitive data exposure during normal user interactions.
R0193.influence: A compromised Web3 dependency or release path can spread asset theft and backdoors across many downstream projects, damaging ecosystem trust.

observables: Newly released dependency packages or wallet plugins are installed by many projects in a short window with author identity diverging from historical records
Build artifact hashes mismatch official releases or the signing chain changes unexpectedly
SDK update logs contain suspicious network callbacks, private-key reads, or dynamic remote code loading
Downstream projects show anomalous authorization, transfers, or sensitive data exfiltration after upgrading a dependency
Package manager resolution logs show internal package names hijacked by same-name external packages
